overview: A condemnation clause in a lease defines the rights of landlords and tenants when all or part of a property is taken by government eminent domain. It typically dictates if the lease terminates, how rent is abated, and how compensation awards are divided, often allowing tenants to claim damages for fixtures, improvements, and "bonus value".
